nodes.description: A patent publication titled "Social medical network for diagnosis assistance" describing a method and system for diagnosis assistance using embedding-based similarity between medical cases and experts.

nodes.entity_id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance
nodes.description: The title of the patent publication US9589231B2, describing a network-based approach to assisting medical diagnosis.
nodes.id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance

nodes.description: A method that exploits similarity between a new medical case and existing medical cases and experts embedded in a common embedding space, supporting query-by-cases and query-by-experts.

A multidimensional space in which existing medical cases, experts, and new medical cases are represented as multidimensional embeddings.<SEP>A common multidimensional space in which new medical cases, existing medical cases, and experts are embedded so their similarity can be computed.

A medical case submitted by a requester for which a diagnosis is sought, embedded in an embedding space.<SEP>A medical case submitted by a requester in a query request, comprising a plurality of records relating to a specific patient, which is embedded in the embedding space.

A set of previously stored medical cases embedded in the embedding space, used for similarity comparison.<SEP>A set of previously stored medical cases embedded in the embedding space, used as candidates when a query-for-cases is selected.

A set of experts embedded in the embedding space who can be matched to a new case and attempt to provide a diagnosis.<SEP>A set of medical experts embedded in the embedding space based on information such as their profile, coded medical procedures performed, authored articles, and linked stored medical cases.

A user who submits a query request including a new medical case and selects from a plurality of query types.<SEP>The user who submits a query request including a new medical case and selects from a plurality of query types.

A query type that returns a subset of existing cases based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and embedded existing cases.<SEP>A query type that returns a subset of existing medical cases based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.

A query type that returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and embedded experts.<SEP>A query type that returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.

A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts differs from the cost for a query-for-cases.<SEP>A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts differs from and is higher than the cost for a query-for-cases, encouraging requesters to try query-by-cases first.
An ontology comprising a set of medical concepts joined by links, used to compute multidimensional representations of medical cases and experts, with each concept corresponding to a dimension.
The medical ontology on which the medical ontology used for embedding is based.
A matrix applied to the multidimensional representation of the new case that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology when computing similarity measures.
One of the categories of concepts included in the medical ontology.

Information associated with an expert, used as a basis for embedding the expert in the embedding space.
Medical procedures performed by an expert, used as a basis for embedding the expert in the embedding space.
Articles authored by an expert, used as a basis for embedding the expert in the embedding space.
An attribute of an expert that, along with rating and follower count, may be used when returning the subset of experts for a query-for-experts.
A rating of an expert that may be used when returning the subset of experts for a query-for-experts.
The number of followers of an expert among users of the system, which may be used when returning the subset of experts for a query-for-experts.
A database from which documents may be returned based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and documents embedded in the embedding space when a query-for-cases is selected.

A plurality of records relating to a specific patient that make up the new medical case, including laboratory test results, images, symptom descriptions, patient monitor results, diagnoses, prescribed medications and treatments.
A type of record that may be included in the plurality of records making up the new medical case.

A system comprising memory storing instructions and a processor in communication with the memory for executing the instructions to assist diagnosis.<SEP>A system comprising memory storing instructions for performing the diagnosis assistance method and a processor in communication with the memory for executing the instructions.
A product comprising a non-transitory recording medium storing instructions that, when executed on a computer, cause the computer to perform the diagnosis assistance method.
A processor that performs at least one of the embedding, providing, returning subsets of cases or experts, and computing the query cost.
A provision for making a payment to an expert for formulating a diagnosis when a query-for-experts is selected.
A component in communication with the memory for executing the stored instructions.
A component that stores instructions for receiving queries, embedding cases, providing query types, and returning subsets of cases or experts.
A network comprising a diagnosis assistance system and a set of user devices for linking requesters and experts with the system.
A set of devices for linking requesters and experts with the diagnosis assistance system.
The determination sought for a new medical case, which an expert attempts to provide.
A representation of a medical case or expert generated in the embedding space.
A query type available at a first cost that identifies a subset of existing cases based on similarity of multidimensional representations.
A query type available at a second cost, higher than the first cost, that identifies a subset of experts based on similarity of multidimensional representations.
